articleTitle: Deterministic Parallel Execution Of Sequential Programs
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: Parallel discrete event simulation (€'DES) research has led to the development of distributed order preserving protocols. Generalization (f these protocols offers the prospect of parallel and yet deterministic execution of sequential program. In this paper we introduce a simple but general method of extracting a logical time coordinate system f.om sequential programs and discuss some of the basic issues in the application of PDES paradigms to general purpose parallel computing.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of A Priority Flow Control Scheme For Multicomputer Networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: The performance of multicomputers is highly dependent on the underlying communication mechanisms, especially for a large-scale multicomputer machine with hundreds or thousands of processing elements. It is often required that an interconnection network of a multicomputer would be able to deliver a guaranteed communication bandwidth for a class of messages, depending on their usages. This paper describes and evaluates a virtual channel flow control algorithm, which can meet low-latency transmission time and high network throughput requirements. We consider a 20 mesh network with eight virtual channels. Performance evaluation results for network of 256 nodes are presented.

articleTitle: Reduced Markov Models Of Parallel Programs With Replicated Processes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: The behaviour of parallel programs with replicated processes is modelled by continuous time Markov chains. For high-level model description, we use stochastic automata networks. We are particularly interested in models of parallel programs which exhibit symmetries. Exact lumpability is exploited for reducing the model’s state space, thus making complex models of large real systems computationally tractable. Complexity analysis of a new reduction algorithm shows that the method can be applied efficiently in practice. Keywords: Parallel Programming, Markov Models, Lumpability, State Space Reduction.

articleTitle: Harp: A Statically Scheduled Multiple-instruction Issue Architecture And Its Compiler
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: This paper presents the results of an investigation into the performance of a new statically scheduled multipleinstruction-issue architecture and its compiler. HARP is a Long Instruction Word Architecture developed in conjunction with a simple compile-time scheduling technique called conditional compaction. The architecture is characterised by a conditional execution mechanism which is used by the scheduler to pack the instructions within aprocedure into long instruction words. The study compares the speedups obtained for the C and Modula-2 versions of a set of short, general purpose, integer benchmarks, running on simulations of the architecture with different functional unit configurations.

publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: This paper describes the architecture and operation of a SIMD massively parallel computer, called associative mesh, based on asynchronous communications, specifically designed for applications in the computer vision domain. Associative mesh is a reconjigurable interconnection whose basic primitives combine communications and computations. We present the associative net and outline its computational model, discuss some implementation issues, and show some application algorithms.

articleTitle: Creatures And Spirals A Data Parallel Object Architecture
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: Creatures, a new class of cellular machine, retains many of the attractive features of Cellular Automata whilst allowing the user to describe dynamic systems an a more intuitive and efficient manner. In order to implement such a machine efficiently a generalisation on the Doubly Twisted Torus has been explored, and routing techniques developed for the surface. Such a surface has improved load balancing properties compared to traditional toroidal surfaces, while retaining the simple embedding of low dimensional structures.

articleTitle: A Large-grain Data-flow Language And Its Control-driven Implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: The paper describes the large-grain data-pow language DSPL and its efficient control-driven implementation. The described language is an integral part of the DSPL programming environment, an integrated approach to design and implement dedicated parallel applications. In order to show the suitability of the DSPL language, we describe how applications written in DSPL can be automatically adapted in order to (mainly) statically implement the design decisions as the process granularity and the execution order. This is important to minimize runtime overhead for scheduling and communication. Different from related work, the DSPL language supports conditional execution of tasks which is present in many applications. The paper addresses the problems encountered with the merger of tasks in the presence of conditional execution.

articleTitle: Zelig: A Novel Parallel Computing Machine Using Reconfigurable Logic
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) can be used in a computing capacity as reconfigurable coprocessors which implement the core functions of an application. This technique of using reconfigurable hardware as introduced as an approach for realising a desirable combination of machine performance, cost and flexibility for certain applications. A novel parallel computer, Zelig, using FPGAs is presented in this paper. The design of the machine is introduced and some comparative results of the machine’s performance are given.

publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: In the last decade, neural nets have gained considerable interest as an alternative means to solve many artificial intelligence problems and related tasks. Neural nets are a very striking example of parallel systems, where the individual components work under local control and cooperate asynchronously. Such net approaches offer tremendous performance speedups, if these organization schemes can be mapped to appropriate hardware building blocks; additionally neural nets possess inherent mechanisms for toler ranting faults of the individual net elements

articleTitle: A Transputer-based Neural Network To Determine Object Positions From Tri-aural Ultrasonic Sensor Data
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: For mobile robot navigation purposes, we use an object position in measurement system. The measurement system is composed of two parts, a signal acquisition part and the signal processing part. The first part consists of three ultrasonic sensors, one transmitting and three receiving. In the second part, the topic of this paper, we use a transputer based neural network to process the acoustical signals from the receivers. We shotu how to combine ultrasonic sensor data with an artificial neural network to estimate object positions (distance rscr; and bearing Theta;). Acoustic signals from the three sensors are preprocessed ana! then passed through the neural network. The object positions are determined by the neural network. Experimental results on object position measurement show that a neural network of the multilayer perceptron type can be trained to do this task, and that the resulting system is reasonably sensitive and accurate.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of Fault Tolerant Structures For Parallel Systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: Computing systems are being used increasingly in applications which demand safe and reliable operation at all times. However, fault-free operation under all operational circumstances cannot be guaranteed. This paper presents an evaluation of fault tolerant structures for parallel systems. A hardware module has been designed and built for this evaluation. It uses the parallel processing device, the transputer, and the software is designed and implemented in occam. A number of tests have been performed on the module, including injected faults in the software, hardware and combinations of both. A number of software fault tolerant strategies are used and some comparative conclusions drawn.

articleTitle: Representation And Measurement Of Non-rigid Egocentric Motion: A Parallel Implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: Computer vision systems are by nature highly computationally intensive and hence their implementation on a parallel architecture is an attractive proposition. In addition many computer vision applications require the use of different types of parallelism (from SIMD to MIMD) at various stages of their processing. In this paper we will examine one such application, that of the analysis, representation and measurement of non-rigid motion in image sequences. In particular we examine how this application can be mapped on to U parallel architecture utilising the most appropriate form of parallelism at each stage.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation Of An Abstract Programming Model For Image Processing On Transputers
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: This paper considers two questions which are currently a matter of debate in the parallel programming community. The first is, to what extent can an abstract, programmeroriented programming model be implemented eficiently on a parallel machine? The second is, given an abstract programming model, is the interpretive abstract machine approach viable as an implementation technique for achieving portability and flexibility with efficiency? The paper addresses these within the speci$c context of image processing applications. It uses the image processing language I-BOL to consider the first question: for the second, it compares two implementation approaches which have been used for I-BOL and a related language: direct compilation, and interpretation of p-code.

articleTitle: Mad-postman : A Look-ahead Message Propagation Method For Static Bidimensional Meshes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: A message-passing network needs some kind of flow control which regulates the allocation of buflers to messages upon its reception and it also blocks any transmission that may cause an overflow. The pow-control technique, implemented in a distributed manner, is fundamental in determining the router internal structure and also the minimum and average latency. Three switching mechanisnis were taking into account in this work, namely: wormhole, cut-through and mad-postman. This paper analyzed and compared by means of a high-level simulation these three mechanisms when applied to 2-0 mesh networks with dimensional order routing. Networks with both bit-serial and parallel links have been considered. Network performance has been measured in terms of the average message latency and the maximum sustained throughput under a random pattern of traffic.

articleTitle: Image Processing on Parallel Machines: A Protocol For Managing Global Objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: The problem considered in this paper is the definition of a control strategy for managing objects spanning over several windows of an image, whenever such windows ae assigned to different nodes of a distributed-memory MIMD parallel machine. The solution here proposed is based on a pyramidal structure of MANAGER processes, which handle communication of data between WORKER processes operating upon adjacent windows in a distributed way, balancing workload and avoiding the need of a centralized controller. Even if the structure is not tailored to a particular image processing algorithm, it will be here be applied - as an example - to a parallel edge detector.

abstract: In this paper a fault diagnosis system for transport electrical grids based on neural networks is presented. l3.e functional modularity adopted in the solution allows to partition the electrical network in a way such that parallel architectures can be used to obtain acceptable response times in realistic operation. Using this type of architecture permits to improve the cost @netion used by experts to determine the faulty element. In order to achieve that, it is proposed to obtain the cost function in a segmented way. The particular characteristics of the power system to monitor will condition the parallel architecture selection.

articleTitle: Distributed Environments & Distributed Program Design
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: This paper presents an overall view about the most common methods for implementing task schemes for process control from the operating system point of view as well as from the Occam point of view. They are discussed and compared an a comparative study. In addition the best known development platforms Helios, ParC, Inmos Toolsets and Parix are introduced. Their significant features are presented and compared in a detailed comparative stttdy focussing the advantages and disadvantages of each development platform with respect to its usefulness in distributed program design. The presented study is addressed to all developers who intend to design distributed software for their transputer based architecture and who are on the outlook for a programming platform that almost suits their needs.

articleTitle: Integrating Memory And Network Accesses : A Flexible Processor-network Interface For Efficient Application Execution
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Second Euromicro Workshop on Parallel and Distributed Processing
abstract: It has been shown that the large communication overhead in current multicomputer systems can be reduced greatly by using proper communication mechanisms [l] and processor-network interfaces [4]. A good processor-network interface design is highly dependent on application characteristics, programming model, memory interface, and routing characteristics of the network. Unfortunately, these issues are not exploited fully in the previous work. In this paper, we address these issues from the perspective of application performance and propose a processor-network interface architecture that to optimize the system performance. Through such a design, not only the processor and network are tightly coupled, also are memory operation and message passing. As a result, high-level operations such as gather and scatter can be supported easily instead of using low level operations proposed previously
